versions.name: RXV2-0.9.235-tx-failsafe
versions.notes: The transmitter's 'send failsafe to receiver' button now works on RXV2 (it was silently ignored): it captures the current channel positions — trims and subtrims included, since they're baked into the radio stream — exactly like the web 'Save failsafe' button. And with the FC-telemetry switch OFF (no flight controller, e.g. a PWM converter), the receiver now STREAMS the captured failsafe posture on CRSF after signal loss instead of going silent and letting the converter drift.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.234-civilised-ota
versions.notes: Civilised OTA (Malcolm's word): when the connection drops during an install — routine over Bluetooth, and at the reboot moment on WiFi — the page no longer cries 'failed'. It says 'Installing… waiting for the receiver to come back', polls until the receiver reappears, and judges by the version it reports: new version = success (auto-reload), same old version = a real failure, still absent after 5 min = 'reload in a moment'.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.233-battery-save-dialog
versions.notes: Fixes the View-channels page broken in 0.9.231/232 (a script error meant Save battery settings did nothing and saved values weren't displayed — the settings themselves were never lost). Battery save now shows a proper 'Saved' confirmation dialog like the gear-ratio save.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.232-live-settings
versions.notes: Reboot only when it's actually needed: changing the CRSF rate, FC-telemetry switch, throttle channel or arming channel now applies instantly ('Saved — applied instantly' on the page, no reboot). Only changing the protocol itself (or PPM polarity) still reboots, because the output pin must be reconfigured.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.231-channels-tidy
versions.notes: Channel assignments consolidated: the arming channel now lives on the Output protocol page beside the throttle channel (one 'Channels' box); the arming card is gone from View channels. Battery card layout fixed so Pin/Ratio/Cells labels stay with their boxes on narrow phone screens.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.230-throttle-safe
versions.notes: SAFETY: the throttle channel (configurable on the Output protocol page, default 3) is held fully LOW (885 us) from power-on until the transmitter is actually heard — a receiver booted without its TX can no longer put the motor at half stick. Plus: booting with the TX already on now leaves Bluetooth open for 30 s (connect in that window and the link stays); and renaming the receiver from the app now works (inline rename box — the old popup was silently ignored by app WebViews).

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.229-vbat-d9-only
versions.notes: Battery divider: D9 only (GPIO 8 — the one free pad on 2-radio boards; D4 carries the status LED), auto-detected when FC telemetry is off. IMPORTANT: replaces 0.9.227/228, which used wrong GPIO numbers for the divider pin (raw 9 = the SPI MOSI line!) — do not use those two versions with a divider.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.227-vbat-adc
versions.notes: Receiver battery voltage on a spare pin: wire the pack through a 220k/10k divider (ratio 23.0, good to 12S; 100k/10k = 11.0 for 6S) + 100nF to D4 or D9 (free on 2-radio boards). Configure on the View-channels page; live volts (and per-cell if you set the cell count) shown there, and the voltage is sent to the transmitter as telemetry (12S pre-halve quirk handled).

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.226-async-update-check
versions.notes: The update check no longer blocks the receiver: manifest fetches now run in the background, so opening the app's front screen can't pause the servo output (the brief servo twitch with no transmitter connected). Results are cached for 10 minutes.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.225-fc-telem-switch
versions.notes: New 'Flight controller on the telemetry line' switch on the Output protocol page. Untick it for plain CRSF-to-PWM servo converters: some echo junk that gets misread as telemetry (phantom current readings / false max-current alarms on the transmitter) — the receiver then ignores the telemetry line entirely and sends no Rotorflight probes. Default remains ON.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.224-crsf-rate
versions.notes: Adds a CRSF frame-rate setting on the Output protocol page (250/100/50 Hz). Lower it to 100 Hz for CRSF-to-PWM servo converters whose firmware misbehaves above ~100 Hz. Default stays 250 Hz. Installing this also updates the web pages.
